name: BERT Large NER
description: BERT Large NER is a state-of-the-art model trained for Named Entity Recognition (NER). Utilizing the BERT architecture, it's capable of identifying and categorizing entities within text into predefined classes. Being a 'large' variant, it has a higher number of parameters which contributes to its ability to understand complex textual relationships. It's highly versatile and can be employed across various domains to extract meaningful insights from unstructured text data.

name: WikiNeural Multilingual NER
description: WikiNeural Multilingual NER is a sophisticated model designed to perform Named Entity Recognition across multiple languages. Built on a robust architecture, it's fine-tuned to identify a wide range of entities in different linguistic contexts. Its multilingual capability makes it a valuable asset for global applications, enabling businesses and researchers to extract and categorize entities from text in various languages seamlessly. The model's performance is commendable, making it a reliable choice for multilingual NER tasks.

name: Biomedical NER All
description: Biomedical NER All is a specialized model tailored for the extraction of biomedical entities from text. Leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, it is adept at identifying a spectrum of biomedical entities including diseases, drugs, and genes. Its training on a diverse range of biomedical literature ensures high accuracy and reliability in entity recognition within the biomedical domain. The model is a significant asset for researchers and professionals in the healthcare and life sciences sectors, aiding in the extraction of valuable insights from biomedical text.

name: BioBERT Chemical NER
description: BioBERT Chemical NER is a finely tuned model dedicated to the task of recognizing chemical entities within text. Drawing from the BioBERT architecture, it demonstrates a high level of proficiency in identifying chemical names, formulas, and other related entities. The model's training on chemical-specific datasets ensures its adeptness in accurately recognizing and categorizing chemical entities, making it a vital tool for researchers and professionals in the field of chemistry and pharmacology.

name: BENT PubMedBERT NER Gene
description: BENT PubMedBERT NER Gene is a specialized model engineered for the recognition of gene entities within text. Utilizing the PubMedBERT architecture, it exhibits a keen ability to identify and categorize gene mentions and related entities in text. Its training on gene-centric datasets ensures a high degree of accuracy in gene entity recognition, proving to be an indispensable resource for genomic research and related fields. The model facilitates the extraction of gene-related information, aiding in the advancement of genomic studies.

name: FoodBaseBERT NER
description: FoodBaseBERT NER is a dedicated model for the recognition of food-related entities within text. With its training on food-specific datasets, it's highly proficient in identifying various food items, ingredients, and culinary terms. The model leverages advanced NLP techniques to accurately recognize and categorize food entities, enabling a comprehensive understanding of food-related text. It's a valuable asset for culinary professionals, food bloggers, and researchers in the food and nutrition domain.

name: Disease Entity Recognition Model
description: The Disease Entity Recognition Model is a fine-tuned Named Entity Recognition (NER) model designed to identify disease entities within text. It leverages the PubMedBERT model and has been fine-tuned on specific datasets including the NCBI Disease Corpus and PHAEDRA to specialize in recognizing diseases, particularly the entity type 'DISO'​1​.
examples: Example usage of this model could include identifying disease mentions in medical texts, clinical notes, or research papers.
usecases: Automating the extraction of disease-related information from medical literature, enhancing information retrieval systems in the biomedical domain, and supporting data curation tasks for medical databases.
